full_judgment:
5. In the year 1922 with the approval of the Assam Government KB Ahia Waqf Estate was established empowering the Government as trustee, As per terms and condition of Waqf deed the present Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet is the ex-officio Mutawalli. The said Waqf Estate is a Waqf-ul-Lillah. The said Kazir Bazar Hat was established in the year 1952 within the khas land of the said Waqf Estate and the Hat and Bazar take place in every Friday and Monday of the week. 

 11. The further case of the petitioner is that Hat/Bazar situated within Sylhet City Corporation could not be legally owned and possessed by the respondent No. 6 due to whole sale acquisition of Khas land by the Government under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Hat and Bazar (Establishment and Management) Ordinance, 1959. The further case of the petitioner is that under section 2(12) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the cattle market is a "Hat" according to the definition of section 20(2a) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The land or structure therein of a Hat or Bazar has been excluded from retainable land and acquirable by the Government. sub-section 2(a) of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have retrospective effect of excluding Hat and Bazar from the category of retainable land and Hat and Bazar vested in the Government from the notification under section 3(2) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1956 and as such no fresh notification is required for inclusion of a Hat and Bazar. The further case of the petitioner is that section 20(5)(i)(c) excludes Waqf land from operation of sub-section (1), (2) and (3) of section 20, those subsections deal with retainable land. The provision of sub-section 6 of section 20 again excludes Hat or Bazar from the operation of sub section (c) of clause (i) of subsection (5) and Clause (ii) of that subsection i.e. Hat/Bazar are not retainable on the ground that those Hat and Bazar are Waqf Estate. 

 12. Further case of the petitioner is that Waqf Estate is not entitled to retain Hat /Bazar. Hat and Bazar land stands acquired on the date of notification under section 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. In the meantime, the Government has not taken over possession of the land of Waqf Estate having Hat and Bazar, the Mutawalli holding right title or any interest in the land having Hat/Bazar continued to manage as the agent of the Government till taking over possession. As per provision of the proviso (i) to section 10(a)(3)(b) no Mutawalli is competent to transfer or create any encumbrance or charge on any such interest over the said khas land in any manner except by a temporary lease not exceeding 1 year. Any transfer or any encumbrances or charge created or any lease given in contravention of the provision is null and void. The provision of section 39(1)(a) is clear with non-obstinate clause that land of Hat and Bazar under Waqf Estate is subject to acquisition and are entitled to compensation. The provision of section 2 of Hat and Bazar (State Acquisition) Ordinance 1959 provides establishment of any Hat and Bazar by any person other than the Government. The Local Administration may establish Hat and Bazar with the prior approval of the Government. Since notification under section 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has already been made. No fresh notification for Acquisition of Hat and Bazar of the Waqf Estate is necessary. Since there is no encumbrance in any manner in the Waqf Estate, even if there is any encumbrance in the property shall be null and void. The nullity of such encumbrance takes effect from the inception that means the encumbrance is void and ab initio. 

 20. Mr TH Khan, the learned Senior Counsel appearing with Mr JN Deb and Mr Helaluddin Mollah and Mr AKM Shamsul Huq by filing affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit in opposition for the respondent Nos. 6 and 7 submitted that the property originally belonged to Khan Bahadur Abu Naser Mohammad Ahia who subsequently in the year 1922 established Waqf Estate as Waqf-ul-Lillah known as KB Ahia Waqf Estate under the approval of the then Government of Asham. Since then the case property along with other properties have been possessing and enjoying by the Waqf Estate. The Secretary, Ministry of Land, Respondent No. 2 also directed to the Deputy Commissioner of Sylhet, Maulvi Bazar, Sunamganj not to disturb the peaceful possession of the Waqf Estate and according to the said direction, the respondent No. 6 Waqf Estate filed Title Suit No. 7 of 2002 for correction of record which is still pending for determination and another Title Suit No.72 of 1999 in respect of permanent injunction was decreed in favour of the Waqf Estate against which no appeal was preferred. The petitioner has no locus standi to file instant writ petition. He further submitted that the property in question is Waqf ul Lillah and the income of the said Waqf-ul-Lillah being used for the benefit of charitable purpose. He further submitted that the whole sale acquisition under section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not applicable in respect of the properties under the Waqf Estate. Moreover, the Government did not acquired the property of the Waqf Estate till today nor the Government paid any compensation or award in favour of the Waqf authority till today nor there was any direction to handover possession of the Waqf Properties. He further submitted that the said Waqf Estate enrolled under Provisional Government of Asam which was subsequently, enrolled after partition of Bengal to the Waqf Administrator of East Pakistan under EC No. 13071 and before declaration of Sylhet Division, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet was the Mutawalli and after declaration of Division the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet became Mutawalli of the said Waqf Estate thus Managing the same, at the same time the Divisional Commissioner became the representative of the Government. Since at the time of SA operation some of the properties of the Waqf Estate was wrongly record in the name of Government as khas Land of the Government, Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet wrote a letter to the Secretary Ministry of Land, the Secretary, Ministry of Religious and the Deputy Commissioner of Sylhet to hold an enquiry and lastly the Divisional commissioner on 8-10-1987 issued a letter under Memo No. Vum-71/87/684 / (1) 4 stating that “এস্টেটের যে সকল সম্পত্তি ভুল ক্রমে সরকারী খাস খতিয়ান রেকর্ড করা হইয়াছে সেগুলি সংশোধনের ব্যবস্থা নিতে অনুরোধ জানাচ্ছে।” 

 23. He further submitted that the respondent No. 6 filed Title Suit No. 7 of 2002 before the Joint District Judge, Habigonj against the Government and others praying for declaration of Title in respect of the suit property including the land in question. The said Title Suit is still pending for final hearing. He further submitted that one of the leasee of the Government i.e. Md Shamsul Alam has filed writ petition No. 5164 of 2003 claiming some land of the Waqf Estate as the leasee of the Government. But the Rule was discharged with cost by the judgment and order dated 29-3-2005. Ministry of Land respondent No. 2 on 3-5-2006 wrote a letter to the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet by canceling their previous letter dated 1-1-2006 in respect of taking over possession of the case properties; which indicates that the property in question is a Waqf Property not Khas land of the Government. He further submitted that the property in question is the property of KB. Ahia Waqf Estate is 100% Waqf-ul-Lillah under section 20(5)(i)(c) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 100% Waqf-ul-Lillah property cannot be taken over by the Government. He further submitted that since there is a judgment and decree of permanent injunction against the Government in Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 in respect of the properties under the Waqf Estate, against which no appeal has been filed and as such the judgment and decree of the Title Suit No.72 of 1999 is binding upon the Government. Another Title Suit No. 7 of 2002 is still pending before the Second Court, Habigonj against the Government of Bangladesh in respect of the Waqf property prying for declaration of title and a such the instant writ petition is not maintainable. He further submitted that the property of the Waqf Estate is not normal. Hat and Bazar, it is the absolute property of the Waqf Estate and has been using for special purpose for cattle market for the people of the locality. Whether the property is normal Hat and Bazar under the definition of Hat, Bazar or not is a question of fact which can be decided in the civil Court not before this writ jurisdiction. 

 34. The filing of the suits with all ulterior motive to continue illegal possession of the property in question, which stood acquired with the publication of the notice under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Any suit filed against the acquisition or any order passed by way of injunction to refrain the Government from taking possession in pursuance of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act abates under PO 19 of 1972. With the publication of the notification under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 all retainable interest including that of the Debutar and Waqf Estate stood acquired and all non retainable khas land also stood vested in the Government. Further stated that the letter dated 8-10-1989 (Annexure-2) and letter dated 5-8-1991 (Annexure-'3') are outcome of manipulation and connivance of some public official being gained over by the interested quarter to continue illegal possession of the cattle market and that no authority can pass any order to give any direction for Acquisition of the property which stood acquired and vested in the Government. The respondent No. 6 has no legal control or possession of the property in question. As per sub-section (2a) of section 20 any land or building in a Hat or Bazar vest to the Government with retrospective effect on the Publication of the notification under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1956, all rent receiving interest including that of Debattar and Waqf Estate stood acquired and all non-retainable khas land also vested in the Government and that the judgment and decree in question abated under PO 19 of 1972 and has no legal force. PO 19 of 1972 creates a complete bar to file a suit by any person or by entertaining any suit by any Court, challenging the validity and legality of any order of Acquisition taken or passed in pursuance of the acquisition under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 46. Md Abdul Hakim Mondal, the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet, Mutawalli of Khan Bahadur Ahia Waqf Estate represented by Md Abdur Rahman filed Writ Petition No. 331 of 2006 before this Court challenging the office Memo No. Vo:Ma/Sha-8/Kha:Ja:Ba:/745 /2005 /02 dated 1-1-2006 issued and signed by the respondent No. 5 Senior Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Land, section-8 stating that the properties in question known as Kazir Bazar Hat is situated under District-Sylhet, Upazilla-Sadar, Mouza-Sylhet Municipal area originally owned and possessed by Khan Bahadur Abu Naser Mohammad Ahia who established Waqf Estate on 16-2-1922 popularly known as KB Ahia Waqf Estate with other property including the present case properties. The said Khan Bahadur Abu Naser Mohammad Ahia executed and registered Waqf deed after obtained prior approval of the then Government of Asham and the terms and conditions as laid down in the said Registered Waqf deed the representative of the Government i.e. revenue head of Sylhet will be Mutawalli/Trustee of the said Waqf Estate and after partition of India, the said Waqf was enrolled as EC No. 13071 in the Office of the Waqf Administrator and before declaration of Sylhet Division, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet was the Mutawalli and after declaration of Sylhet Division as per terms of the deed, the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet being revenue head of Sylhet Division has became the Mutawalli of the said Waqf Estate and till today he is managing and controlling the properties of the said KB Ahia Waqf Estate. Before declaration of the Sylhet Division the property was managed and looked after by the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet and the said Deputy Commissioner was the representative of the Government. Subsequently, some portion of the land of the Waqf Estate was wrongly recorded in SA Khatian as khas land and in respect of wrong recording the Secretary, Ministry of Land, the Secretary, Ministry of Religious and the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet and Waqf Administrator made several correspondence letter to hold an enquiry and lastly on 8-10-1987 vide Memo No. Vum-71 /87/684/91) 4 issued by the Secretary Ministry of Land stated that- 

 52. The respondent No. 1 appeared and filed affidavit-in-opposition stating that Kazir Bazar Hat is situated at Mouza-Sylhet Municipality under Sylhet Sadar, District- Sylhet with an area of 1.553 acres which was owned by khan Bahadur Abu Naser Md Ahia. After obtaining approval from the then Government of Assam on 16th February, 1922, he made Waqf Eitate Known as KB Ahia Waqf Estate with the case properties along with other land measuring total area of 24,000 acre which was executed and registered on 16-2-1922. Afterwards the said Estate was enrolled as EC No. 13071. According to the terms of the said deed the representative of the Government revenue head i.e. the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet will act as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate. After declaration of Sylhet Division, the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet became a Mutawalli of the said Waqf Estate who is managing and controlling the said properties. Further stated that some of the land of the KB Ahia Waqf Estate was wrongly record in the name of the Government in Khatian No.1 as Khas land, Afterwards, the Ministry of land issued Memo dated 8-10-1987 for correction of record and also memo No. Vu;Ma:/Sha/5/ Waqf/Sylhet/ 177/91 (3) dated 5-8-1991. But the Deputy Commissioner, Habigonj, Sunamganj and Moulvibazar tried to disturb the properties of the Waqf Estate. As a result, one of the beneficiary of the Waqf Estate Shahid Mubarak instituted Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 before the Court of learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet. The said suit was decreed with permanent injunction but no appeal has been preferred against the said decree. The petitioner has been possessing the properties and spending the income accumulated from the properties in various charitable purposes. The Waqf Estates are not acquirable by the Government as per section 20(5)(4)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and as such the petitioner executed a lease deed of the properties as mentioned and possessing the same. 

 58. The Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 filed by one Shahid Mubarak, a beneficiary of KB Ahia Waqf Estate is contrary to the clear provision of PO 90 of 1972 and, as such, decree has no legal force. Further stated that the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Habigonj has no territorial jurisdiction to entertain any suit against the Deputy Commissioner of Sylhet, Sunamganj and Moulvibazar. The so called decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge automatically abates in view of PO. 90 of 1972. The Courts are in complete bar to entertain any suit by any person challenging the legality or validity of the acquisition or any order passed in pursuance of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and that the Divisional Commissioner (Writ Petitioner) Ex-officio Mutawalli has no legal authority to manage and control the property already vested in the. Government by operation of law and that all the rent receiving interest including the properties of the Waqf Estate and Debuttor vested in the Government. The retrospective amendment made by Ordinance No. XII of 1960 in section 20 by the incorporation of sub-section (2a) which has effect of excluding hats and bazars in the khas possession of the rent receivers became vested in the Government from the date of notification in 1956 under sub-section 2(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 (3) Such Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee shall, as the agent of the Government, be entitled to collect, at the rates provided in. and subject to the provisions of, sub section (4), all rents and cesses payable by the tenants to the Government in respect of such interests, and to collect the usufruct of such interest in Khas land for the period from the date of acquisition of such interests till the last day of the agricultural year [or till the exercise of the right of possession, as referred to in sub-section (2) whichever is later] and to retain the proceeds of such collection [or other income] in lieu of ad interim payments under section 6A in respect of such interests and his remuneration, subject to payment to the Government annually, in the prescribed manner, of a sum equivalent to the total of the following amounts, namely— 

 (i) No such Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee shall be entitled to transfer, or to create any encumbrance or charge on, any such interest in any khas land in any manner otherwise than by a temporary lease but no such temporary lease shall be given for a period exceeding one year at a time expiring on the last day of the agricultural year in which it is 'created, nor shall any tree be cut down or building demolished, except with the previous permission of the Collector and on such terms as the Collector may prescribe in that behalf; and any transfer or any encumbrance or charge created or any lease given in contravention of the provision thereof  shall be null and void and the full value of any tree cut down or building demolished in such contravention shall be recoverable from the Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee as an arrear of rent or land revenue; 

 (i) No such Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee shall be entitled to transfer, or to create any encumbrance or charge on, any such interest in any khas land in any manner otherwise than by a temporary lease but no such temporary lease shall be given for a period exceeding one year at a time expiring on the last day of the, agricultural year in which it is created, nor shall any tree be cut down or building demolished, except with the previous permission of the Collector and on such terms as the Collector may prescribe in that behalf; and any transfer or any encumbrance or charge created or any lease given in contravention of the provision thereof shall be null and void and the full value of any tree cut down or building demolished in such contravention shall be recoverable from the Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee, an arrear of rent or land revenue;"
